Senses.Explanation: The death-flinging stance Chan rows demand before the thinking mind can step in. Guting Shanjian, instructing his trainee, rules that knowing life-and-death to be this perilous, one must through all twelve hours disregard danger and death, cast body and life away, and see the matter through to a verdict; Yingshan Zhiyin, on the dragon-boat festival, grants that even the tide-players fling peril aside and smash their cauldrons, then asks how much more the great matter of life and death deserves it; Hanyue Fazang gives the portrait of one who does — a mallet to the mouth before the question, front teeth on the ground, a sword at the brow, blood spattering the Brahma heaven; and Wuyi Yuanlai, at the same festival, sets the pearl under the dragon's jaw and rules it must be snatched heedless of danger before a hand can land on it. Lianyue Daozheng lets Yangqi's three-legged donkey tread down Xuanzha's tiger and asks who, not heeding danger and death, will save it, snapping that the sweet melon is sweet to the stem; Lianfeng Su's elite striver drills bone for marrow atop Vairocana's crown, slices flesh to blow on the hair at the master's heel, enters with a single blade, and becomes blind-donkey seed; Zhufeng Zhenxu, enthroned at the old man's call, claims the stance for himself — heedless of danger and death he opens the alms-bowl there and raises the Tiantong principle and the Zhaojue gate; and Liao'an Qingyu conjures just such a reckless fellow bursting out to rule that his own Benjue verdict also deserves the twenty staves, ordering the incense attendant to arrange it.
